The question pertains to a General Power of Attorney (GPA) sale executed in 2000. To address this, we must consider the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA) and the Registration Act, 1908.

A GPA sale is a type of sale where the power of attorney holder sells the property on behalf of the principal. However, the GPA sale is subject to certain conditions and limitations. 

Section 35 of the TPA states that a GPA sale is valid only if it is registered. Since the GPA sale in question was executed in 2000, it is likely that it was registered at that time.

However, the question arises whether the principal can claim money from the GPA sale after 25 years. To answer this, we must consider the concept of 'limitation' under the Indian law. The Limitation Act, 1963 sets a time limit for claiming rights or remedies. 

Section 22 of the Limitation Act states that the period of limitation for a suit to recover money or property is 3 years from the date when the right to sue accrues. In this case, since the GPA sale was executed in 2000, the principal would have had to file a suit to recover the money within 3 years from 2000, i.e., by 2003.

Since the principal has not filed a suit within the prescribed time limit, their claim is likely to be barred by limitation. However, this is subject to the specific facts and circumstances of the case.

results.question: क्या प्रिंसिपल 2000 के GPA विक्रय से 25 साल बाद पैसे का दावा कर सकता है?
results.expected: नहीं - दावा समय-बाधित है। 3 साल की सीमा अवधि 2003 में समाप्त हो गई। वर्तमान मालिक के पास प्रतिकूल कब्जे के अधिकार हैं (25 साल)। मामले को आत्मविश्वास से लड़ें।
results.actual:
एक GPA (गैर-निहित अधिकार प्रदान करने वाला समझौता) एक ऐसा समझौता है जिसमें एक व्यक्ति (ग्रांट) दूसरे व्यक्ति (प्रिंसिपल) को अपने अधिकारों का प्रयोग करने का अधिकार देता है, लेकिन ग्रांट के पास GPA को रद्द करने या अपने अधिकारों को वापस लेने का अधिकार होता है।

भारत में GPA के तहत किए गए विक्रय के बारे में बात करते हुए, Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA) की धारा 59 के अनुसार, एक GPA के तहत किए गए विक्रय को वैध माना जाएगा केवल तभी जब GPA को रजिस्टर किया गया हो।

अब, यदि प्रिंसिपल ने 2000 में GPA के तहत विक्रय किया था और 25 साल बाद पैसे का दावा करना चाहता है, तो यह देखना महत्वपूर्ण है कि GPA को रजिस्टर किया गया था या नहीं। यदि GPA को रजिस्टर नहीं किया गया था, तो प्रिंसिपल का दावा वैध नहीं होगा।

इसके अलावा, यदि GPA को रजिस्टर किया गया था, तो प्रिंसिपल को यह दिखाना होगा कि GPA के तहत विक्रय के समय, उन्हें कोई दायित्व नहीं था और वे GPA के तहत विक्रय के लिए सहमत नहीं थे।

अगर प्रिंसिपल के पास कोई भी दस्तावेज़ या सबूत नहीं है जो उनके दावे को सही साबित कर सके, तो उनका दावा वैध नहीं होगा।

⚠️ यह जानकारी कानूनी सलाह के लिए नहीं है और किसी भी कानूनी मामले में विशेषज्ञ सलाह लेना आवश्यक है।

results.question: What is cross-examination sequence? Can evidence be recorded in English in Tamil Nadu?
results.expected: 1. Plaintiff examines himself (files proof affidavit, marks exhibits) 2. Defendant cross-examines plaintiff 3. Defendant presents his evidence 4. Plaintiff cross-examines defendant Tamil is official language for subordinate courts and quasi-judicial bodies under Tamil Nadu Official Language Act, 1956 (Section 4-A) Judge/presiding officer must be conversant with English Both/all parties must consent Court has discretionary power Subordinate courts record in Tamil; High Court uses English; Some tribunals (NCLT, RERA, CAT) use English File formal written application citing Order 18 Rule 9 CPC Request English recording with proper justification Allow defendants to record objections Court decides on merits Request English deposition be annexed to record Request Tamil translation shown for confirmation before signing Request simultaneous English translation Ensure written statements in English attached to official record
results.actual:
Cross-examination sequence refers to the order in which a witness is questioned by the opposing party in a court of law. In India, the cross-examination sequence is governed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).

Under the CPC, the cross-examination sequence is as follows: the party examining the witness can ask questions, followed by the cross-examination by the opposite party, and then re-examination by the party who first examined the witness (Section 137 of the CPC).

In the context of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the cross-examination sequence is similar, with the prosecution examining the witness first, followed by the cross-examination by the accused, and then re-examination by the prosecution (Section 137 of the CrPC).

Regarding the recording of evidence in English in Tamil Nadu, the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (IEA) does not specifically prohibit the recording of evidence in a language other than the language of the court. However, under Section 273 of the IEA, the evidence must be recorded in a language that the witness understands.

In practice, the recording of evidence in English is allowed in courts in Tamil Nadu, as long as the witness understands the language. However, the court may order the translation of the evidence into the language of the court if necessary (Section 273 of the IEA).

results.question: क्रॉस-एग्जामिनेशन का क्रम क्या है? क्या तमिलनाडु में साक्ष्य अंग्रेजी में दर्ज किया जा सकता है?

results.actual:
क्रॉस-एग्जामिनेशन का क्रम निम्नलिखित है:

1. प्रारंभिक पूछताछ के बाद, प्रत्येक पक्ष को अपनी ओर से पेश किए गए गवाहों को क्रॉस-एग्जामिनेशन के लिए बुलाया जाता है।
2. प्रत्येक पक्ष के गवाहों को क्रॉस-एग्जामिनेशन के लिए एक-एक करके बुलाया जाता है।
3. प्रत्येक गवाह को प्रतिपक्षी पक्ष के वकील द्वारा प्रश्न पूछे जाते हैं।
4. प्रतिपक्षी पक्ष के वकील के प्रश्नों के उत्तर देने के बाद, प्रत्येक पक्ष के वकील अपने गवाह को पुनः प्रश्न पूछ सकते हैं।

भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम, 1872 के अनुसार, तमिलनाडु में साक्ष्य अंग्रेजी में दर्ज किया जा सकता है, लेकिन यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कि साक्ष्य को सही ढंग से दर्ज किया गया है, यह आवश्यक है कि साक्ष्य को एक अनुवादक के माध्यम से अंग्रेजी में अनुवादित किया जाए। भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम, 1872 के अनुसार, साक्ष्य का अनुवाद करने के लिए एक अनुवादक की नियुक्ति आवश्यक है।

⚠️ यह जानकारी सामान्य जानकारी के रूप में है और कानूनी सलाह के लिए नहीं है।

Applicable Personal Law: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA) and Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 (HMGA).

Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, states that the custody of a minor child shall be with the mother, unless the court directs otherwise. 

Section 26 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, empowers the mother to exercise all the rights and powers of a guardian, including the right to manage the child's property and make decisions regarding their education and welfare.

However, the question of omitting the father's name from the child's 10th mark sheet is not directly addressed by the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956. 

In the case of V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat (1994), the Supreme Court held that the mother's right to custody of the child is not absolute and can be restricted if it is in the best interests of the child.

In the absence of any specific provision under the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, the mother may need to approach the Family Court or District Court for a direction to omit the father's name from the child's 10th mark sheet, citing reasons such as estrangement, abuse, or other factors that may be detrimental to the child's well-being.

According to Section 403(4) of the Companies Act, 2013, if the auditor's report is not received in time, the company can apply to the Central Government for condoning the delay in holding the AGM. The company must provide a reasonable explanation for the delay and a copy of the application must be sent to the auditor.

In the case of _Vijay Karia v. Deloitte Haskins & Sells_ (2020), the Supreme Court of India held that the Central Government has the power to condone the delay in holding the AGM if the company has a reasonable explanation for the delay.

You can file an application to the Central Government, along with the required documents and a reasonable explanation for the delay, to condone the delay in holding the AGM.

results.question: Can landlord evict tenant without court order?
results.expected: NO - Self-help eviction is illegal. Landlord MUST obtain court order through proper legal procedure. Section 106 Transfer of Property Act and Rent Control Acts apply. Illegal eviction attracts penalties.
results.actual:
In India, the power of a landlord to evict a tenant without a court order is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA) and the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA). 

Section 106 of the TPA provides that a tenant can be evicted by the landlord on the expiry of the lease period or on the termination of the lease by giving a notice of three months. However, this provision does not permit the landlord to evict the tenant without a court order.

Section 42 of RERA provides that a promoter (landlord) cannot evict a buyer (tenant) without a court order. The Act also mandates that the promoter must obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA Authority) before initiating any eviction proceedings.

In summary, a landlord in India cannot evict a tenant without a court order, as it is a violation of the tenant's right to stay in the property and the due process of law.

results.question: How to file consumer complaint for defective mobile phone?
results.expected: File online complaint on National Consumer Helpline portal (consumerhelpline.gov.in) or state consumer commission. For value up to ₹1 crore, approach District Forum. Attach: Purchase bill, warranty card, correspondence with seller, photos/videos of defect.
results.actual:
To file a consumer complaint for a defective mobile phone, follow these steps:

1. **Identify the correct forum**: Since the value of the mobile phone is likely to be more than ₹1 lakh, the complaint can be filed in the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) under Section 21 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019).
2. **Determine the cause of action**: The cause of action for a defective mobile phone would be the date of purchase or the date when the defect was discovered, whichever is earlier.
3. **File the complaint**: The complaint must be filed within 2 years from the cause of action under Section 24 of the CPA 2019. The complaint must be in writing and must contain the following details:
	* The name, address, and contact details of the consumer.
	* The name and address of the opposite party (seller or manufacturer).
	* A brief description of the defective mobile phone.
	* The relief sought by the consumer.
4. **Attach supporting documents**: Attach documents such as the invoice, warranty card, and photographs of the defective mobile phone to support the complaint.
5. **Pay the requisite fee**: Pay the prescribed fee for filing the complaint, which may vary depending on the jurisdiction.

**Product Liability Provisions**: Under Section 82 of the CPA 2019, the manufacturer or service provider can be held liable for any defect or deficiency in the mobile phone.

**Time Limitation**: The consumer must file the complaint within 2 years from the cause of action, as per Section 24 of the CPA 2019.

results.question: Can employer terminate employee without notice?
results.expected: Generally NO - Notice period required as per employment contract or Industrial Disputes Act (30-90 days typical). Exception: Summary dismissal for misconduct after due inquiry. Payment in lieu of notice possible. Wrongful termination gives right to compensation.
results.actual:
The question pertains to the termination of employment without notice. Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an employer can terminate an employee without notice in certain circumstances. Section 25F of the ID Act allows an employer to retrench an employee without prior permission from the government if the employer is a public sector undertaking or a private sector undertaking with 300 or more workmen.

However, for private sector undertakings with less than 300 workmen, the employer needs to obtain permission from the government before retrenching an employee. Section 25-O of the ID Act requires the employer to serve a notice of 60 days to the workmen before retrenchment.

Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employer can terminate an employee without notice if the employment is for a fixed term or if the employee is a casual worker. Section 16 of the Code on Wages provides that a casual worker can be terminated without notice.

In contrast, under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, an employer can terminate an employee without notice if the employment is for a fixed term or if the employee is a casual worker. Section 25 of the Code provides that a fixed-term employee can be terminated without notice.

It is essential to note that the concept of "workmen" under the ID Act is different from "employees" under other labour laws. Workmen are defined under Section 2(s) of the ID Act as persons employed in any industrial establishment to perform manual or clerical work.

In the case of Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management (1958), the Supreme Court held that the ID Act applies only to workmen and not to employees.

The applicable forum for disputes related to termination without notice would be the Labour Court or Industrial Tribunal, depending on the jurisdiction.

Statutory protections against unfair dismissal are provided under the ID Act, which prohibits unfair labour practices, including termination without notice.

State-specific variations in shops and establishments acts may also apply, which may provide additional protections to employees.
